builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
summary: It replaces repeated per-decision invocation of an LLM reasoner with a small fast System-1 policy guided by a modular harness (procedures, state memory, world models) built and revised asynchronously by the LLM, with utility-driven retrieval. The cost is a two-model architecture: harness storage and retrieval, an extra training/serving path for the System-1 model, continued (though declining) System-2 revision calls, and the engineering complexity of feedback-driven module updates. It can fail when the harness accumulates stale or incorrect modules, when utility retrieval selects misleading context on novel states, or when System-2 revisions degrade rather than improve decision quality.
rationale: The approach directly targets the reader's cost and latency constraints by amortizing LLM calls, but the claimed gains are workload-specific and the recursive self-improvement loop needs validation on the reader's own decision tasks before production adoption.
technique: Recursive LLM-built decision harness for fast System-1 agent

claims.statement: It replaces repeated per-decision invocation of an LLM reasoner with a small fast System-1 policy guided by a modular harness (procedures, state memory, world models) built and revised asynchronously by the LLM, with utility-driven retrieval. The cost is a two-model architecture: harness storage and retrieval, an extra training/serving path for the System-1 model, continued (though declining) System-2 revision calls, and the engineering complexity of feedback-driven module updates. It can fail when the harness accumulates stale or incorrect modules, when utility retrieval selects misleading context on novel states, or when System-2 revisions degrade rather than improve decision quality.

Paper claims JevRSI matches or surpasses LLM agents in several settings on three datasets while preserving low-latency execution, with System-2 interventions decreasing over time, amortizing System-2 costs; no single quantified factor is given in the abstract.
